comment: The comparison states that one component controls syntax and the other controls semantics. This is an oversimplification. Information models also carry semantics through element definitions, context, constraints, relationships, and terminology bindings, while syntax usually concerns technical representation.

anchor.note: p.68 l.Lines 674-679 read as the printed page; section 3.5.3.1 agrees

public.text: The comparison states that one component controls syntax and the other controls semantics. This is an oversimplification. Information models also carry semantics through element definitions, context, constraints, relationships, and terminology bindings, while syntax usually concerns technical representation.
public.suggestedRevision: Replace the syntax-versus-semantics distinction with structure and contextual meaning versus coded concept meaning. State that both contribute to semantic interoperability.
